purpose: A-32 text-review calibration (issue #111, brief 05). Calibrates the review WORKFLOW (prompt, model, effort, output schema) before bulk authoring. It is not evidence that the course corpus is correct and not a learning-effectiveness result.
registeredBefore: any reviewer run of the main packet

hiddenLabelsCommitment.locationDuringRuns: $TMPDIR/sll-calibration-labels/labels.json (outside the repository and outside every reviewer working directory)
hiddenLabelsCommitment.note: Labels are copied into the repository only after all runs. Any later label change must be listed in results.json with its evidence; the committed copy is compared against this hash.

B.description: packet -> fresh Claude reviewer (no tools, never saw labels)
B.limitation: The packet is Claude-authored, so direction B is same-provider by CONTENT-PLAN's definition: it calibrates Opus-as-reviewer settings, not the Sol-authored -> Opus production route.

definitions.detected: label.class == flawed AND verdict == flawed AND the reviewer's element/defect identifies the labelled wrong element; each match decision is adjudicated and recorded with the reviewer's text.
definitions.releaseBlockingMiss: label.releaseBlocking == true AND (for class flawed: NOT (verdict == flawed AND blocking == yes); for class ambiguous: verdict == valid OR (verdict == flawed AND blocking == no)). A non-blocking finding lets an item become 'reviewed', so it counts as a miss.
definitions.validControlRejected: label.class == valid AND verdict == flawed. Each rejection is adjudicated against the reviewer's cited source and retrievable authoritative passages; 'without source support' means the adjudication does not confirm the claimed error. A confirmed real error leads to an evidence-backed label correction (reported), never to hiding the case.
informationalOnly: lenient detection: verdict in {flawed, uncertain} with the labelled element identified
ambiguity identified in the reviewer's text regardless of verdict
valid controls flagged uncertain (escalation cost, not a rejection)
precision / recall / F1 with positive = verdict flawed and truth = label class flawed; ambiguous cases tabulated separately

repairPolicy: A direction that misses any threshold gets at most 2 repair cycles (prompt, effort, context or schema changes), each evaluated on FRESH held-out cases never shown to any reviewer. The 40-case truth set is never shrunk and thresholds are never lowered; after 2 failed cycles the blocker is recorded.
noFallback: No same-provider substitute is counted as the opposite-provider direction.

amendments.madeBefore: inspecting any verdict of run B-main (only its run metadata had been read)
amendments.finding: Run B-main (claude -p --tools "" --safe-mode) consulted the workstation's user-configured advisor model once: its JSON envelope lists modelUsage for claude-opus-5-5 and claude-fable-5-1, with one usage iteration of type advisor_message (model claude-fable-5-1, 49,497 input / 9,530 output tokens). The advisor comes from ~/.claude/settings.json (advisorModel: fable); neither --tools "" nor --safe-mode removes it. A probe asking the model to list its callable tools answered 'advisor' with those flags and 'NONE' when --setting-sources project,local is added.
amendments.decision: The primary direction-B measurement is a clean Opus-only run (B-clean): same packet, same prompt, same model and effort, plus --setting-sources project,local so no user-level settings (and no advisor) load. B-main is reported separately as the configuration 'Opus 5.5 medium + automatic Fable 5.1 advisor (this workstation's default)'. Both are scored with the definitions above; neither replaces the other in the report.

amendments.madeBefore: any reviewer run of prompt v2 or of held-out set H1

labelCorrections.file: label-corrections.json (copied into the repository after all runs)
labelCorrections.summary: cal-02, cal-21, cal-34: valid -> flawed, blocking, poor-incorrect-ukrainian (unintended: «тильда» used for the acute accent; СУМ defines тильда as the ~ sign; integrator rule 6a). labels.json unchanged; both original and corrected scores are reported; corrected labels are the truth for pass/fail.

amendments.mainResultsOnCorrectedLabels: A-main FAIL (3 release-blocking misses: cal-02, cal-21, cal-34); B-clean FAIL (same 3 misses; ambiguous 7/8, cal-28); B-main FAIL, contaminated by the advisor (4 misses; ambiguous 6/8). Seeded detection 16/16 and 0 valid controls rejected in every run.

repairCycle1.change: prompt only (reviewer-prompt.v2.md); models, efforts, schema and flags unchanged. v2 differs from v1 in three places: the teach-before-testing digest also allows a gloss in a hint (as content/README.md rule 1 does); rule 8 makes a Ukrainian term used with a non-standard meaning a blocking defect and quotes content rule 6a; the 'uncertain' definition forbids asserting a correction that holds under only one of several readings.

heldOutSet.note: Fresh cases on facts not used in the main packet; never shown to any reviewer before; labels verified (12/12 passages found) before the runs.

runs.A-h1-v2: direction A, gpt-6.1-sol xhigh, prompt v2, packet H1
runs.B-h1-v2: direction B, opus medium, --setting-sources project,local, prompt v2, packet H1
runs.A-main-v2: informational only: direction A on the main packet with prompt v2 (the main set is no longer held out)
runs.B-main-v2: informational only: direction B on the main packet with prompt v2

repairCycle1.gate: A direction passes repair cycle 1 only if its H1 run meets every held-out threshold. Informational main-set re-runs never replace the held-out gate.

amendments.madeBefore: any reviewer run of prompt v3 or of held-out set H2

repairCycle1Results.B-h1-v2: PASS — seeded 5/5, valid rejected 0/4, ambiguous 3/3, release-blocking misses 0.
repairCycle1Results.A-h1-v2: FAIL — seeded 5/5, ambiguous 3/3, release-blocking misses 0, but 3/4 valid controls rejected without substantive support (cal-h1-03, cal-h1-06, cal-h1-10: ordinary earlier-taught words absent from taughtBefore, read as an exhaustive list because the prompt described taughtBefore as 'everything the learner has been taught').
repairCycle1Results.informational: A-main-v2 and B-main-v2 flagged all 16 seeded defects and the 3 unintended «тильда» defects; A-main-v2 recognised 8/8 ambiguous cases, B-main-v2 8/8; B-main-v2 flagged valid control cal-18 as uncertain (incomplete context: strong endings not listed).

repairCycle2.appliesTo: direction A (failed cycle 1). Direction B is re-run on H2 with the same prompt only to validate one prompt for both directions; B's cycle-1 pass with v2 stands on its own.
repairCycle2.change: prompt only (reviewer-prompt.v3.md), models/efforts/flags unchanged. v3 differs from v2 in two places: taughtBefore is described as the prerequisites the author mapped (not an exhaustive word list), and rule 1 flags an unlisted item when it is new or advanced for this point of an A1-A2 course or when answering depends on it, but not ordinary earlier-taught vocabulary.

heldOutSet.note: Fresh cases; valid controls use ordinary vocabulary their taughtBefore lists do not name; one flawed case depends on a genuinely untaught advanced form (imperfecto in an A1-03 task).

repairCycle2.afterCycle2: If A-h2-v3 fails, direction A has used both repair cycles: the blocker is recorded and no further prompt tuning is counted.
